title: DNA Extraction and Quantitative PCR Detection of Verticillium dahliae from Soil
author: David Wheeler
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.vwie7ce
materials: MP FastDNA™ SPIN Kit for Soil

DNA Extraction Kit: MP FastDNA™ SPIN Kit for Soil (MP Biomedicals; cat no.: 116560200; cost is $230-290 for 50 reactions or 25 soil samples). 100 ml of 100% ethanol ( not included in the kit ) needs to be added to the concentrated SEW-M solution prior to use. Twice as much lysing matrix E (MP Biomedicals; cat no.: 116914050) is used as compared to other kit components.
Pre-grind the samples in a FastPrep-24 5G (MP Biomedicals; cat no.: 116005500 ) for 40 sec at a speed setting of 6.0.

Post-DNA Isolation Inhibitor Removal: OneStep™ PCR Inhibitor Removal Kit (Zymo Research; cat no.: D6030; $102 for 50 reactions or 50 soil samples). Note: The Zymo columns used for removal of the inhibitors contain a wet matrix. Consequently, it may be necessary to spin briefly the columns for 2-3 sec before use if the matrix is adhered to the cap or if most of it is in the upper portion of the tube.

Standard Curve: A standard curve should be included with every qPCR run. Extract V. dahliae genomic DNA from mycelia or conidia grown in pure culture. Quantify DNA with the Qubit Fluorometer (ThermoFisher Scientific; cat no.:Q33226) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Another fluorometric quantification method can be used, but UV-absorbance-based quantification should not be used. Prepare a ten-fold serial dilution of DNA to use as the template for the standard curve.. The DNA concentration should range from 0.5 ng DNA/µl to 0.5 fg DNA/µl A no template (water) control should also be included with every qPCR run.

Thermal Cycler Conditions (Applied Biosystems StepOnePlus Real-time PCR System; cat no.:4376600) 10 min @ 95°C 40 cycles of 30 s @ 95°C, 30 s @ 60°C, and 30 s @ 72°C (measure data). Melt curve analysis from 60°C, gradually increasing 0.3°C/s to 95°C.

steps.title: Prepare and Dry Soil Samples
steps.instruction: Combine soil cores, air-dry them, and process through a No. 10/2.0 mM sieve.

substeps.instruction: Store dried soil in a cool dark place; if using a fridge, use sealed plastic bags to prevent moisture absorption.

steps.title: Freeze and Lyophilize Soil
steps.instruction: Freeze a 5-10 g soil subsample and then freeze-dry it.

substeps.instruction: Place 5-10 g of soil into a 15 or 50 ml conical polyethylene tube.
Cover the tube with a KymWipe to allow air/moisture movement while keeping the sample contained.
Freeze at -80°C for at least 3 hours.
Freeze-dry under vacuum using a lyophilizer until dry (typically 4 to 24 hours, depending on soil type).

steps.title: Prepare Lysis Tubes
steps.instruction: Set up two lysing matrix E tubes per soil sample to extract DNA from a total of 1 gram of soil.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 mg of freeze-dried soil to each of the two tubes.
Add 828 µl of sodium phosphate buffer (kit supplied) to each tube.
Add 150 µl of nonfat powdered milk suspension (133 mg/ml) to each tube.
Add 122 µl of MT buffer (kit supplied) to each tube.

steps.title: Homogenize and Clarify Lysate
steps.instruction: Homogenize the samples and remove debris via centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Homogenize in the FastPrep machine for 40 seconds at speed setting 6.
Centrifuge at 14,000 X g for 10 min.
Transfer the supernatant to clean 2.0 ml microfuge tubes.
Add 250 µl PPS (Protein Precipitation Solution) and mix by inverting the tube 10 times.
Centrifuge at 14,000 X g for 5 minutes to pellet the precipitate.

steps.title: Bind DNA to Silica Matrix
steps.instruction: Pool the supernatants and bind the DNA to the binding matrix.

substeps.instruction: Shake the binding matrix suspension to re-suspend and add 1.0 ml to a 15 ml tube (one tube per soil sample).
Add the supernatants from the protein precipitation step to the 15 ml tube, avoiding any precipitate.
Invert by hand for 2 min to allow DNA binding.
Place tubes in a rack for 5 minutes to allow the silica matrix to settle.

steps.title: Wash and Concentrate Matrix
steps.instruction: Clean the silica matrix and transfer it to a spin filter.

substeps.instruction: Carefully pipette out and discard 0.75 ml of the supernatant without disturbing the silica matrix.
Gently re-suspend the binding matrix in the remaining supernatant by pipetting.
Transfer 600 µl of the mixture to a spin filter and centrifuge for 1 min at 14,000 X g.
Empty the catch tube and add 500 µl more of the re-suspended silica matrix mixture.
Repeat the transfer and centrifugation process until all silica matrix mixture has been added to the spin filter.

steps.title: Wash Silica Pellet
steps.instruction: Wash the pellet using SEWS-M buffer.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µl of prepared SEWS-M (ensure ethanol was added before use) and gently re-suspend the pellet using the liquid force from the pipet tip.
Centrifuge at 14,000 X g for 1 minute and empty the catch tube.
Add 500 µl of prepared SEWS-M (re-suspension not necessary).
Centrifuge at 14,000 X g for 1 minute and empty the catch tube.

steps.title: Dry the Spin Filter
steps.instruction: Remove residual alcohol from the filter.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge without liquid at 14,000 X g for 2 minutes.
Discard the catch tube and place the spin filter in a new clean catch tube (kit provided).
Air-dry the spin filter for 5 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Elute DNA from Matrix
steps.instruction: Release the DNA from the binding matrix.

substeps.instruction: Gently re-suspend the binding matrix in 100 µL DES (molecular-grade water).
Incubate at 55°C for 5 min in a heat block.
Centrifuge at 14,000 X g for 1 min.

steps.title: Prepare HRC Columns
steps.instruction: Prepare the sample columns according to manufacturer instructions.

substeps.instruction: Snap off the base and remove the green cap.
Insert into a collection tube.
Spin in a microcentrifuge at exactly 8,000 X g for 3 min.
If the HRC matrix is dry, add 400-600 µl water prior to prepping the column.

steps.title: Final DNA Purification and Storage
steps.instruction: Pass the DNA suspension through the prepped column and store.

substeps.instruction: Move the prepped column to a 1.5 ml centrifuge tube.
Add the DNA suspension from the elution step to the prepped sample column.
Centrifuge at 8,000 X g for 1 min.
Store the DNA in the freezer at -20°C.

steps.title: Quantitative PCR Detection
steps.instruction: Analyze samples in triplicate using 20 µl reactions and average the data.
